name: Sign-Up
summary: Covers the user journey from finding Taskly in the app store through completing account creation. The biggest friction point is the registration form, which asks for information users are not ready to provide before they have seen the product.

stages.name: Download App
thoughts: Will this actually help me stay organised?
Is this free or does it cost money?

emotions.label: Neutral
emotions.description: Cautiously optimistic — aware from past experience that productivity apps rarely stick

painPoints: App store screenshots do not clearly show core features
Unclear whether premium features require a subscription
opportunities: Update store screenshots to highlight top three use cases
Add a free-tier badge to the store listing to reduce subscription anxiety

stages.name: Open App
actions: Opens app for the first time
Decides whether to sign up or explore first
thoughts: Can I see what it looks like before creating an account?
I hope this is not another long sign-up process

emotions.label: Neutral
emotions.description: Tentatively engaged — willing to proceed but quick to abandon if the next step feels heavy

painPoints: No guest or preview mode — users must sign up before seeing the product
Welcome screen is generic and does not communicate the core value proposition
opportunities: Offer a 'Try without signing up' guest mode
Replace generic welcome copy with a single concrete benefit statement

stages.name: Create Account
actions: Optionally fills in job role and team size fields
Submits form and waits for verification email
thoughts: Why do they need my job role just to use a to-do app?
I have to verify my email before I can do anything?
Can I just sign in with Google?

emotions.label: Neutral
emotions.description: Willing to complete the form but friction from unnecessary fields dampens enthusiasm

painPoints: Form asks too much upfront — job role, team size, and use-case fields are not required to create an account
Email verification adds a step before the user has experienced any value
opportunities: Allow social login via Google or Apple to reduce form friction
Defer optional profile fields to an in-app prompt after first use
Move email verification to a background step and let users proceed immediately

insights.text: 6 of 8 test participants tried to tap a 'Continue with Google' button that did not exist on the sign-up screen
Sign-up completion rate drops by 34% when the job role and team size fields are shown — removing them in an A/B test recovered the drop-off
4 of 8 interview participants said they had previously downloaded a task manager app and deleted it within a week — initial trust in the category is low
